power_methodology.producer: WattTime (lead; Pixel Scientia Labs and Global Energy Monitor co-credited). v5.11.0 sector citation: Freeman, J., Rouzbeh Kargar, A., Couture, H., Jeyaratnam, J., Lewis, J., Alvara, M., Koenig, H., Nakano, T., Davitt, A., Lewis, C., and McCormick, G. (2025). 'Power sector: Emissions from Electricity Generation.' WattTime, USA; Pixel Scientia Labs, USA; Global Energy Monitor, USA. TransitionZero co-authored the 2024 Remote Sensing paper and was a founding member on the 2019 Google.org power-plant grant but is not credited in the current power citation.
inputs: Plant inventory: coordinates, fuel, prime mover, cooling type, nameplate capacity (Global Energy Monitor trackers, WRI Global Power Plant Database, OpenStreetMap organised-editing campaign 2020-2023)
Satellite imagery: PlanetScope (~3 m RGB+NIR), Sentinel-2 (10-60 m, 13 bands), Landsat 8 OLI + TIRS thermal; indices HOT, whiteness, NDVI, ND-SWIR, ND-TIR
Signal: water-vapour plumes from natural-draft cooling towers and wet-FGD stacks; weather screens
Models: gradient-boosted trees + CNNs; per-image on/off classification (>5% CF) and capacity-factor regression; aggregation to 30-day capacity factor
Training: reported hourly generation (US, Europe, Australia); validation Turkiye, India; US emissions via EPA CAMPD
Emissions = capacity x capacity_factor x country/fuel/prime-mover emission factor
Non-satellite statistical models and meta-modeling from other inventories for plants without plume coverage (satellite method covers ~32% of global power CO2)
Reported accuracy (2024 paper): generation RMSE 1.75 TWh, CO2 RMSE 2.18 Mt, Pearson r 0.80 CF / 0.93 generation / 0.90 CO2
power_methodology.confidence_rating: Qualitative per-source, per-month, per-gas ratings (very high / high / medium / low / very low) in <subsector>_emissions_sources_confidence.csv for: source_type, capacity, capacity_factor, activity, each gas's emissions_factor and emissions, total_co2e_100gwp, total_co2e_20yrgwp. No confidence at country/sector/subnational level. Rubric mapping method to rating is in sector methodology PDFs on GitHub (not fetched).

consumer_attribution: No datacenter, electricity-consumer or grid-load subsector exists. Buildings = onsite fuel combustion only (Duke University; Microsoft TEMPO building volume since v5.11.0). 'Other energy use' is country-level only. HOWEVER: since v5.11.0 (24 Sep 2026) the oil-and-gas production/transport, aluminium and pulp-and-paper subsectors 'now report Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions separately'; and Climate TRACE 'offers Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions factors for hundreds of facilities' with steel factors 'differentiated by regional grid electricity mix and marginal electricity emissions rate' (TASA case study, 17 Jun 2025). So facility-level Scope 2 attribution of purchased electricity is an established pattern that a datacenter subsector could reuse. How Scope 2 is encoded in the CSV columns is unconfirmed.

contribute_route.notes: Support Us page 'Contribute Data' section lists three routes: (1) 'Identify facility level errors' via the share-feedback link on each source card; (2) 'Model new emissions sectors' - notes railways and fluorinated gases have only national-level estimates and invites contact 'about joining the coalition or supporting our work'; (3) 'Donate training or validation data' (non-public data accepted). All go through the contact form (fields: Name, Email, Organization Name, Subject, Message). coalition@climatetrace.org is the data-questions/errors address in the data guide. No published written criteria for new sectors or membership. WattTime is the coalition secretariat; co-founders Gavin McCormick (WattTime ED) and Al Gore. Each sector family is owned by one member org that authors the methodology PDF on github.com/climatetracecoalition/methodology-documents; natural owners for a datacenter subsector: WattTime (power, marginal emissions, hyperscaler data) with Duke (buildings) and Global Energy Monitor (asset inventory + ownership).
